phishing.title: Phishing Attack
phishing.description: Phishing is a social engineering attack where attackers disguise as trustworthy entities to steal sensitive data such as login credentials, credit card numbers, or personal information.
phishing.counter: Always verify the sender's email address. Look for HTTPS and valid certificates. Never click links in unsolicited emails. Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) on all accounts.

malware.title: Malware / Trojan
malware.description: Malware is malicious software designed to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems. Trojans disguise themselves as legitimate software to trick users into installing them.
malware.counter: Keep your operating system and software updated. Use reputable antivirus software. Avoid downloading files from untrusted sources. Scan all downloads before opening.

sql_injection.title: SQL Injection
sql_injection.description: SQL Injection is a code injection technique that exploits vulnerabilities in web applications by inserting malicious SQL statements into input fields, potentially exposing or destroying database contents.
sql_injection.counter: Use parameterized queries and prepared statements. Implement input validation and sanitization. Apply the principle of least privilege to database accounts. Use a Web Application Firewall (WAF).

spoofing.title: Email Spoofing
spoofing.description: Email spoofing is the forgery of an email header so the message appears to come from someone other than the actual source. It's commonly used in phishing campaigns and business email compromise (BEC) attacks.
spoofing.counter: Implement SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records for your domain. Train employees to verify sender identity. Use email authentication tools. Report suspicious emails to your IT team.

cryptojacking.title: Cryptojacking
cryptojacking.description: Cryptojacking is the unauthorized use of someone's computing resources to mine cryptocurrency. It can slow down devices, increase electricity costs, and shorten hardware lifespan.
cryptojacking.counter: Use browser extensions that block mining scripts. Monitor CPU usage for unexplained spikes. Keep software updated. Use ad-blockers that detect mining code.
